Industries

The same obligation.
Very different hazards.

Occupational health obligations are written generally and applied specifically. These are the sectors we work in most, and what usually dominates the risk picture in each.

Manufacturing & FMCG

Production-line ergonomics, noise and chemical surveillance, shift-fatigue management and on-site clinic cover.

Construction & Infrastructure

Work-at-height and confined-space medicals, site first aid capability, standby cover for peak phases.

Oil, Gas & Petrochemicals

Remote-site medical cover, medevac planning, biological monitoring and emergency responder fitness.

Pharmaceutical & Chemical

Exposure-specific biological monitoring, cleanroom health protocols and occupational disease investigation.

Logistics & Transport

Driver medical fitness, sleep apnoea screening, fatigue and journey-management risk programmes.

Corporate & Services

Display-screen ergonomics, mental health and coaching programmes, executive health checks.

Hospitality & Food

Food-handler medical certification, dermatological screening and periodic re-examination.

Energy & Utilities

Electrical-work medical standards, emergency response training and site crisis planning.

Multi-site employers

One protocol set. One employee record. One reporting calendar.

Programmes that were designed for a single plant tend to fracture when they are scaled to five. We define up front what is held centrally and what each site owns.

  • A shared protocol library, versioned centrally
  • Site-level scheduling with a group reporting cycle
  • Consistent fitness criteria across every location
  • Group-level trend reporting for central HSE and HR
  • A single point of contact for contract and escalation

Contractor and turnaround cover

Short-duration, high-density work

Shutdowns, turnarounds and construction peaks concentrate risk into a few weeks and multiply headcount on site. We mobilise temporary site clinics, standby ambulance cover and contractor medical screening for exactly that window.

  • Contractor fitness screening at gate-in
  • Temporary site clinic set-up and staffing
  • Standby paramedic and ambulance cover
  • Demobilisation records handed over on close-out
